according to their similarities. For data given in form of a
similarity graph, this problem can be restated as follows: we want to
find a partition of the graph such that the edges between different
groups have a very low weight (which means that points in different
clusters are dissimilar from each other) and the edges within a group
have high weight (which means that points within the same cluster are
similar to each other). In this section we will see how spectral
clustering can be derived as an approximation to such graph
partitioning problems. \\

import re

def _extract_freetext_problems(self, text: str):
    """
    Catch problem descriptions that appear as plain paragraphs
    (not inside any \\begin{problem}...\\end{problem} env),
    identified by \\ba...\\ea blocks that follow a paragraph
    containing 'mincut', 'cut', 'partition', etc.
    """
    # Match: a paragraph ending with \ba ... \ea
    pattern = re.compile(
        r'(?P<preamble>[^\n]{20,600}?)'   # lead-in sentence(s)
        r'\\ba\s*(?P<body>.*?)\\ea',       # \ba body \ea
        re.DOTALL
    )
    counters = getattr(self, '_freetext_problem_counter', 0)
    objects = []
    for m in pattern.finditer(text):
        preamble = m.group('preamble')
        body = m.group('body')
        combined = preamble.strip() + ' ' + body.strip()
        counters += 1
        obj_id = 'P' + str(counters)
        clean_text = self._clean_latex_to_text(combined)
        assumptions, conclusions = self._split_assumptions_conclusions(clean_text)
        obj = Problem(
            id=obj_id,
            kind='problem',
            index=counters,
            label=None,
            name=None,
            raw_latex=combined,
            clean_text=clean_text,
            env_name='freetext_ba',
            assumptions=assumptions,
            conclusions=conclusions,
        )
        obj._source_pos = m.start()
        objects.append(obj)
    self._freetext_problem_counter = counters
    return objects

    prefix = config['id_prefix'] if config else 'P'
    obj.id = prefix + str(counters['problem'])
    obj = Problem(
        id=obj.id,
        kind='problem',
        index=counters['problem'],
        label=obj.label,
        name=obj.name,
        raw_latex=obj.raw_latex,
        clean_text=obj.clean_text,
        env_name=obj.env_name,
        assumptions=obj.assumptions,
        conclusions=obj.conclusions,
    )
    obj._source_pos = source_pos
